features.quote: Cap turns (e.g., 40) — necessary anyway since degenerate loops run forever.
features.justification_quote: The cap is itself a measurement (turns-to-degradation, censored at cap), so it's not pure cost-cutting.

features.quote: stop optimizing for reproduction rate as the primary objective. It's the wrong target and it's actively misleading.
features.justification_quote: A test that breaks everything 95% of the time has near-zero discriminating power

features.quote: if you optimize knobs for reproduction rate, you'll find the settings that break it and then report 'high degradation rate' as if it were a property of the model.
features.justification_quote: The next model regresses or improves and your engineered-to-break tasks may not move at all, or move for reasons unrelated to the actual robustness change.

features.quote: Once this is a regression gate, there's pressure to train against it... you'll likely teach models to suppress visible self-criticism rather than actually become more robust
features.justification_quote: Keep a held-out variant of the task families that never feeds back into training so you can tell genuine improvement from gaming the metric.
